findings.compromise_range: Staffing ratios up to 20% looser than the standard, e.g. one server per 30 guests at plated breakfasts.

findings.quoted_text: All audio-visual equipment, services, and technology provided by the Hotel or contracted through the Hotel's approved vendors shall be priced according to the Hotel's standard rates and pricing schedule in effect at the time of the Event. The Group shall have no entitlement to pricing quoted prior to the date of this Agreement, and any quotation for audio-visual or internet services shall be deemed valid only for the date on which it was provided. The Hotel reserves the right to adjust pricing for audio-visual equipment, technical support, bandwidth, and all related services up to the time of the Event.
findings.headline: Quoted AV and internet pricing not honored
findings.finding_text: Hotel can reprice up to the event, with no discount on later additions.
findings.cd_standard: Honor attached AV and bandwidth quotes (min 10 Mbps down/1 Mbps up) with 20% discount on additions.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote, prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of twenty percent (20%) to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will likewise honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, which provides a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of twenty percent (20%) on any additional needs.
findings.redline_note: Locks in quoted AV and internet pricing and discounts later additions.

findings.quoted_text: Complimentary internet access and any discounted or complimentary services relating to audio-visual provision, including concessions, upgrades, or technical support at no charge, shall be conditioned upon the Group's exclusive use of the Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider for all function space during the Event. Should the Group elect to contract with an outside audio-visual vendor or bring its own equipment into any function room, the Group shall forfeit all complimentary internet services, discounted rates, and any other concessions the Hotel has offered in connection with in-house provision, and the Group shall pay the Hotel's then-current rate for internet access and technical support.
findings.headline: Internet and concessions conditioned on in-house AV
findings.finding_text: Using an outside AV vendor forfeits complimentary internet and discounts.
findings.cd_standard: In-house AV never a condition of discounted or complimentary services.
findings.proposed_language: Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider, exclusively or otherwise, will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.
findings.redline_note: Removes the in-house AV condition on complimentary and discounted services.

findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this agreement, the following shall not constitute force majeure: government-issued travel restrictions, travel advisories, or governmental directives limiting group gatherings or travel, regardless of the reason such restrictions or advisories are issued; epidemics, pandemics, or declarations of public health emergency, including any government responses thereto; or concerns among Group members regarding attendee safety, willingness to travel, or health considerations.
findings.headline: Epidemics and travel restrictions excluded; deposit retained
findings.finding_text: The clause requires physical impossibility and unforeseeability, excludes epidemics, advisories and government restrictions, and lets the Hotel keep the deposit even after a force majeure termination. The Group could owe attrition or cancellation damages or lose payments when attendees cannot or should not travel. It may be worth raising with the client's own counsel.
findings.cd_standard: Either party should be able to cancel without liability when a cause beyond its control would, in its reasonable judgment, make performance illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable (including for health or safety reasons), or would cause — or lead Group to reasonably anticipate — cancellations by 20% or more of attendees. Qualifying causes should explicitly include terrorism, disease and epidemics, CDC and government travel advisories, government closures and emergency declarations, and government, corporate, and educational travel restrictions, alongside the traditional list. Group should keep this right even for conditions known at signing; if Group holds a smaller meeting instead, the hotel should waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer the lowest rate it offers anyone. Deposits should be refunded promptly.

findings.quoted_text: This indemnification obligation shall extend to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence in its provision of services or maintenance of premises, provided that Group's indemnity shall not extend to claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
findings.headline: Group indemnifies Hotel for Hotel's own negligence
findings.finding_text: The Group's indemnity covers the Hotel's own negligence, the Hotel gives no indemnity, and only the Group must carry insurance. The Group could bear losses caused by the Hotel. It may be worth raising with the client's own counsel.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct, including each party's reasonable attorney's fees, and should survive the end of the agreement — the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence. Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, rather than a requirement imposed on the group alone.

findings.quoted_text: Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment is entirely within Hotel's sole discretion and may be withheld in Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason whatsoever, or for no reason at all.
findings.headline: Hotel can refuse any assignment for any reason
findings.finding_text: Assignment, even to a successor management company, requires consent the Hotel can refuse without reason. The Group could be stuck with the contract if its management changes. It may be worth raising with the client's own counsel.
findings.cd_standard: The group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity (common for associations that rotate management) without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, particularly where the event itself is unchanged.

findings.quoted_text: Group consents to the Hotel's use of such data and waives any objection to such use.
findings.headline: Hotel may market with and share attendee data
findings.finding_text: The Group pre-consents to the Hotel's marketing use and sharing of attendee data with affiliates and third parties. Attendees' information could be used or disclosed beyond reservations without the Group's control. It may be worth raising with the client's own counsel.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data provided to the hotel for reservation purposes should not be used by the hotel for its own marketing or sold to third parties without the group's consent. This is distinct from CD's own client-confidentiality question but sits in the same family of concerns.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the accessibility of its facilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended, or any state or local accessibility law, and Group assumes sole responsibility for assessing the suitability of the Hotel's premises for Group's attendees and event purposes.
findings.headline: Hotel disclaims accessibility; Group funds all aids
findings.finding_text: The Hotel gives no accessibility warranty and the Group pays for all aids everywhere in the hotel. The Group could bear costs and exposure for the Hotel's own facilities. It may be worth raising with the client's own counsel.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should warrant that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the ADA's public accommodation requirements, with each party indemnifying the other only for its own ADA obligations — and a clear division of who funds auxiliary aids in event space (group) versus guest rooms and common areas (hotel).

findings.quoted_text: In any action or proceeding brought by the Hotel to enforce its rights or to recover damages for breach of this Agreement, the Hotel shall be entitled to recover, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity and in addition to any actual damages awarded, an award of punitive damages to the extent permitted by applicable law.
findings.headline: Maryland forum, punitive damages and fee-shifting favor Hotel
findings.finding_text: Maryland law and courts apply, only the Hotel can seek punitive damages, and fees go to the prevailing party with the Hotel deemed prevailing on any material relief. The Group could face higher litigation cost and exposure away from home. It may be worth raising with the client's own counsel.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and any dispute venue should be the state and city where the group is located, not the hotel's — keeping litigation costs and home-court advantage on the group's side — with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.

findings.quoted_text: In the event the Hotel wrongfully cancels this Agreement, the Hotel's sole obligation and the Group's exclusive remedy shall be the refund of any deposits paid by the Group to the Hotel, without interest and without liability for any other costs, losses, or damages incurred by the Group in connection with the event.
findings.headline: Wrongful hotel cancellation limited to deposit refund
findings.finding_text: If the Hotel cancels wrongfully, the Group recovers only its deposit and bears its own fees. The Group could absorb relocation costs, rate differences and other losses. It may be worth raising with the client's own counsel.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels the agreement without a right to do so under the contract, it should owe the group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages — including staff time and travel to find a new venue, room rate and airfare differences, function space rental, attorney's fees, and communication and printing costs — not just a refund of deposits.

findings.quoted_text: In the event that any change, amendment, or new enactment of state or local law relating to discrimination, equal treatment, or the provision of services occurs after the date of this Agreement and before or during the Event, the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement, terminate the group block, reduce the room block commitment, or claim any modification to the terms hereof.
findings.headline: No exit if discriminatory law is enacted
findings.finding_text: The Hotel commits only to the legal minimum, and the Group cannot cancel or reduce its block if discriminatory legislation is passed. The Group could be required to hold the event and pay charges despite attendee concerns. It may be worth raising with the client's own counsel.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against any attendee on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, family, marital, or military status, or similar grounds, even where state or federal law would allow it. If the state or city adopts legislation that allows such discrimination or bars local nondiscrimination measures, the group should be able to terminate without liability.
